title: Paying for police dispatch of by-law enforcement
subtitle: Neighbourhood association affiliations for 2026 and a second adjournment of two development charge complaints.
overview: The committee recommended that Council enter into a formal agreement with Waterloo Regional Police Services, Waterloo, Cambridge and North Dumfries for dispatch of municipal by-law officers, as long as Waterloo and Cambridge take part {{vote:m5}}. Police have provided this service without charge or a written agreement for decades, but changes to provincial policing legislation now let them recover costs. Staff said the cost is built into the 2026 budget through by-law revenue, but it will be reviewed each year and could rise.

The committee added a direction that staff write to the police service and the police board asking for collaboration with City staff on matters affecting city services. Members said the main reason to proceed was the safety of by-law officers, who rely on police for information about people and properties.
The committee also recommended approving the 2026 list of neighbourhood associations for affiliation and for the City's third-party liability insurance program {{vote:m1}}.

Separately, the committee granted a second request to adjourn hearings on two development charge complaints until no later than March 9 {{vote:m2}}. Because of that, the staff alternatives to dismiss the complaints as late were not put to a vote.

decisions.item: Police dispatch agreement for by-law enforcement
decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council support a formal dispatch services agreement with Waterloo Regional Police Services and the other municipalities, provided Waterloo and Cambridge participate, with the Mayor and Clerk to sign it to the City Solicitor's satisfaction {{vote:m5}}.

decisions.item: Letter to police service and board
decisions.detail: As an amendment to the dispatch motion, the committee directed staff to write to the police service and the police service board requesting collaboration with City staff on matters affecting city services.
The committee recommended approving the proposed neighbourhood associations for 2026 affiliation and adding them to the City's third-party liability insurance program {{vote:m1}}.

debate: Several councillors called the new charge a form of downloading from police onto municipalities and described it as nickel-and-diming, noting it comes from the same taxpayers. Some tied it to other recent police and regional cost increases.

Staff and councillors said the deciding factor was officer safety. Only police hold flags on people and properties, and no other dispatch provider can access that information, so the alternatives would cost about the same while reducing safety.

Councillors asked about future costs. Staff said the fee is based on call volume, will be reviewed annually, is covered in 2026 by higher by-law revenue, and could affect taxes if it grows. The agreement is to include a clause allowing the City to withdraw, and staff will report back on call data.

Several councillors wished police representatives had attended to explain the timing and reasoning. One suggested building a service standard for call pickup times into the contract, since staff said there was no recourse on response times.
Some members wanted better collaboration between the City, the region and the police, and one suggested looking at the full cost of services Kitchener provides to the region.
